answer.summary: All three, each scoped. Derive the fact when it is actually stored, and derive it correctly. Generate permitted fictional detail once and persist it, so the same question gets the same answer next time. Never fabricate source evidence. And refuse only the specific action that genuinely needs the missing information, rather than the surrounding system — an approved game profile is not blocked because exact-law research is incomplete, missing artwork does not invalidate a person or a meeting, and a missing balance is not zero. What the player is shown is the practical meaning of the gap; internal ids belong in developer information.

answer.stillOpen: Answered in four sentences inside a short-answers block rather than as a worked contract, so the boundary cases our record listed are settled by principle rather than case by case. The entry carries a delivery-wide caveat that it is source inspection and a systems brief, with no production code, merge or coefficient approved.

notes: This is a design question rather than a factual survey, filed here because no explicit research has been done on it and the owner's instruction is to defer such things rather than hold them.
It is not asking what any particular rule should be. It is asking for the policy that decides, so the next fifty cases are decided once rather than one at a time by whoever meets them.

An answer that says 'it depends, and here is what it depends on' is the best possible outcome. A single blanket rule is almost certainly wrong, because refusing a legal requirement we cannot source and refusing a modder's content pack are not the same act.
question: When the game needs a fact it does not have, when should it refuse to act, when should it assert a default and carry on, and when should it re-derive the fact from material it already holds? What distinguishes the three cases, and what must a refusal tell the player?

sourcesChecked.source: The four states unblocked on 2026-09-22 — Alaska, Nebraska, Minnesota and Ohio — and the candidate-qualification refusal path they all ran through
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: All four refused, and all four refused for a reason about the repository rather than about the candidate: a missing commencement date, a requirement stated in months the code read in years, a compiler token the parser did not know. That establishes the refusal discipline is worth its cost for legal requirements. It says nothing about where else the same discipline applies, and three of the four looked like ordinary bugs from the screen.

sourcesChecked.source: The same evening's counter-examples, in the same repository
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: An unanswered job offer asserted a start date that had gone stale and quoted it months later. An education release label was guessed, which disabled the refusal that would otherwise have fired. Nebraska and Minnesota were settled by re-deriving from pages already held, in under an hour. Three different answers to the same question, none of them chosen deliberately, and each defensible in isolation.

sourcesChecked.source: The owner's own ruling on content packs, 2026-09-22: 'ignore it and say so. that shouldnt hold the game back.'
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Settles the case where the missing thing is a modder's work: load what is understood, skip the rest, and state what was skipped. It cannot be generalised as it stands, because the cost of being wrong about a modder's field is an afternoon, while the cost of being wrong about a state's eligibility rule is the game asserting something false about the real world.

sourcesChecked.source: src/simulation/candidate-qualification.ts and the four-state research typing it implements
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Implements KNOWN, UNKNOWN, NO_REQUIREMENT_FOUND and NOT_APPLICABLE, and holds the line that unknown is not permission. It is the machinery for whatever answer this question produces; it does not choose the policy, and it currently exists in only one corner of the game.

title: When a missing fact should refuse, assert or be re-derived
usableAnswer: A short policy with a test somebody can apply at a call site without knowing this history. Ideally: the question to ask of a missing fact, the answer that sends it to each of the three outcomes, and what a refusal owes the player — whether naming the gap, offering the action anyway with a marker, or something else. Worked against the cases in the checked list would be ideal, and disagreeing with how any of them was decided is a useful answer, not an awkward one.
whyItMatters: Four cases in one evening across four independent lanes decided this differently, and none of them decided it on purpose. The refusals were right and cost four states their playability until found; the assertion was wrong and quoted a stale date at the player for months of game time; the guess was the worst, because it disabled the guard silently and nothing would have announced it. This is not a question about one rule. Every registry the game is about to fill for fifty-one jurisdictions will meet it, and the answer decides what happens in the far more common case where a row is simply absent.
